issues.description: The solution's Animal class and its subclasses define constructors that take (String name, int age) whereas the problem description and the template Main use single-argument constructors (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")). This constructor-parameter mismatch means students following the problem/template (or using the provided Main example) will be unable to instantiate the solution classes or will be confused about required constructor parameters.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signatures consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement and template Main to require and demonstrate two-parameter constructors (String name, int age) and document the additional 'age' attribute; or (B, preferred) modify the solution to use single-argument constructors (String name) for Animal and its subclasses (remove the age attribute and related constructor parameter), so the solution matches the UML, problem text, and the template example.

issues.description: The problem UML and description specify that Animal has a name attribute only, but the solution's Animal class introduces an additional 'age' attribute (int age) with getters/setters. This extra attribute diverges from the specified design and can confuse students about which attributes they must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem UML by removing the extra 'age' attribute from the Animal class (and its getters/setters), or alternatively update the problem statement and UML to include and describe the 'age' attribute and require constructors to initialize it. Prefer removing 'age' from the solution so it matches the provided UML and template examples.

issues.description: The problem specification and the template Main show animals constructed with a single String name (the UML and the commented Main use e.g. new Seal("Clarabelle")). However, the solution adds an extra attribute 'age' to Animal and implements constructors for Animal and its subclasses that require (String name, int age). This divergence (presence of the 'age' attribute and the two-argument constructors in the solution vs. the one-argument constructors implied by the problem/template) creates a mismatch students cannot easily reconcile and will cause compile errors using the provided Main example.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor/attribute design consistent across artifacts. Either (A) remove the extra 'age' attribute from the solution's Animal and change subclass constructors to single-argument constructors (String name) so they match the UML and template Main, or (B) update the problem statement UML and the template Main to include the 'age' attribute and show constructors taking (String name, int age), and add getAge()/setAge() to the problem specification. Ensure the same constructor signatures (parameters and attribute names) are used in problem, template, and solution.
